title: Cross-Border Clearinghouse for VTuber Merch
one_liner: A duty-paid storefront and fulfillment rail for VTuber agencies that pre-sells to overseas fans and clears unsold Japanese inventory to them.
customer: Mid-size and independent VTuber and idol agencies (not Cover or Anycolor initially), plus overseas fans buying from a duty-paid storefront.
problem: Cover Corp's FY3/2026 revenue rose 13.7% but net profit fell 45.7%, hit by 1.8B yen of unsold merch and a 3.3B yen metaverse write-off. Overseas viewers are about 30% of viewership and roughly 10B yen of revenue, yet those fans face customs surprises, region-locked stores and 30-100% proxy markups.
solution: A global storefront and fulfillment layer with duty-paid shipping, pre-order demand aggregation, and Japanese warehouse partners. Overseas pre-order counts feed manufacturing quantities to reduce overproduction. Overstock is bought or consigned and resold to overseas fans with authenticity guarantees.
why_now: The US ended its $800 de minimis exemption in Aug 2025 and the EU is moving the same way, which breaks the old cheap-parcel proxy model. Hololive's profit drop is a public case study in overproduction.
revenue_model: 15-25% commission on gross merchandise value plus fulfillment fees, and 25-40% of wholesale margin on bought overstock.
non_obvious_insight: Overproduction in Japan and unmet demand overseas are two sides of one imbalance. Forecasts miss overseas demand because logistics hide it, so a clearinghouse converts waste into revenue and generates a better forecast from pre-orders.
first_30_days: Contact 10 small VTuber agencies and 3 Japanese merch producers. Launch a 50-SKU duty-paid shop for one agency. Line up a Japan-based fulfillment partner and pre-sell to an overseas fan community.

title: Percentage-Rent Rails for Small Retail Strips
one_liner: Sales-linked leases with rent automatically swept from the tenant's POS, so independent landlords can fill dark restaurant and shop spaces and tenants stop dying under fixed rent.
customer: Owner-operator landlords of neighborhood retail strips and mixed-use buildings with vacancy, and independent restaurants and retailers seeking space. Platform revenue comes from landlords and processed rent.
problem: Higher rates and a squeezed consumer are closing independents. Landlords face 6-12 months of vacancy and costly tenant improvements. Percentage-rent leases align risk, but small landlords do not trust tenants' sales reports, so the structure has been confined to big malls.
solution: A standard 'base plus percent' lease template (a lower base of about 50-60% of market plus 5-8% of gross sales above a breakpoint). Rent is computed and swept automatically from Toast, Square or Clover data with tenant consent, and the landlord sees a live dashboard. Add leasing and brokerage, and a lender-facing cash-flow report so landlords can refinance on more predictable income.
why_now: Refinancing at higher rates pushes landlords to prefer occupied space. Rates just rose again and the consumer is K-shaped. POS APIs and embedded payments now make sales reporting verifiable and rent collection automatic for small operators.
revenue_model: 1-2% of rent flow processed, a leasing commission on placements, and a lender-reporting subscription. Optional financing spread for landlords.
non_obvious_insight: Percentage rent died in small retail because of an information problem, not an economics problem, and POS data solves the information problem. Because landlord income scales with tenant sales, the system flips the landlord from adversary to partner and wins in booms as well as downturns.
first_30_days: Recruit three landlords with vacant restaurant or retail spaces in one metro. Have a lawyer draft the lease template. Build Toast and Square OAuth plus ACH sweeps with existing tools. Sign two tenants on sales-linked leases and use their first rent runs as proof.

title: Withholding-Credit Reconciliation for Indonesian Sellers
one_liner: Reconcile marketplace-withheld tax against annual returns for the many small sellers across Shopee, TikTok Shop and Tokopedia.
customer: Indonesian SME marketplace sellers and the bookkeepers who serve them.
problem: Indonesia starts marketplace tax collection on Oct 1 and has cut de minimis to $3. Sellers on several platforms will see withheld amounts on payouts, and matching those to annual filings creates over- and under-payment risk.
solution: Ingest payout statements and withholding proofs by API or WhatsApp forward, reconcile per platform, flag threshold crossings and generate return workpapers. The wedge is a white-label tool for accountants who serve seller communities.
why_now: The Oct 1 start date forces this pain within a quarter. Details of the rules should be verified before building.
revenue_model: Rp99-299k per month per seller, or an accountant white-label licence.
non_obvious_insight: Platform collection makes compliance visible, and a seller's first pain is reconciling rather than filing. The accountant channel is fragmented and unserved.
first_30_days: Support one platform's statement format and recruit 50 sellers through seller WhatsApp groups.

title: Won-Bid Price Benchmark Co-op for Cleaners
one_liner: An anonymous give-to-get database of what jobs actually sold for, so specialty cleaners and similar trades can price with market data instead of cost-plus calculators.
customer: Owner-operators of bid-priced service trades. Start with post-construction, commercial and janitorial cleaning, then pressure washing, window cleaning and junk removal. They pay $19-29/mo. Later buyers are the suppliers and insurers who want price indexes.
problem: Every month r/sweatystartup fills with the same question: "What's the going rate for commercial cleaning?", "How to price a large post-construction cleaning job (30k sqft+)", "Pricing on 55,000 sq foot machine shop cleaning", "I need help with quote calculator!", "How do you price your cleaning jobs? Looking to update my rates". The cluster scores 85/100 in an August 2026 snapshot. Calculators only give a cost-plus floor.
solution: A contribution flow accepts anonymized won and lost bids (scope, sqft, frequency, ZIP-3, price, outcome). Owners can also upload old proposal PDFs or emails, and an LLM extracts the structured fields so contributing is one step. In return they see the p25/p50/p75 price band and a win-rate curve for their scope and region. Later it adds a bid sanity check that reads quotes exported from Jobber or Housecall Pro, and a published quarterly price index.
why_now: LLM extraction from messy PDF quotes, emails and photos removes the data-entry burden that killed earlier crowd-pricing efforts. Owners now ask peers on Reddit and also ask ChatGPT, which only gives generic ranges. Rising labor and insurance costs make owners want to reprice, and they need market data to do it safely.
revenue_model: Free to contribute and see coarse bands. $19-29/mo for full bands, win curves and quote checks. Enterprise data licensing, such as a price index for distributors, insurers and franchisors, from $500/mo once there are at least 1,000 bids.
non_obvious_insight: Cost-plus tells you the price floor, not what the market paid, and that is the number people are asking about. The demand for pricing tools is huge but formula-only: the Method Clean Biz janitorial bid calculator says it has been "used by over 170,000 cleaning professionals over the past 10 years" and uses a cost-plus formula with no market data (https://methodcleanbiz.com/janitorial-bid-calculator/). Yet owners still ask peers about going rates. r/sweatystartup has six pricing threads in one snapshot (https://www.ideafast.pro/pains/sweatystartup). Nobody publishes won-bid prices, so the only way to get them is a co-op where contributors trade their own data. The business is the dataset, and the first 200 contributed bids are a moat.
first_30_days: Week 1: set up a Typeform and a Google Sheet. Answer pricing threads in r/sweatystartup and cleaning forums with "send me your last few bids anonymized and I'll send back the market band". Weeks 2-3: collect 100+ bids by doing the analysis by hand and publish a free weekly "price index" post. Week 4: ask the first 30 contributors to pay $19/mo for continued access, and start building the PDF proposal extractor.

title: Same-Day Sub and Coach Bench for Home Daycares
one_liner: A membership that guarantees a licensed home daycare a vetted substitute within hours and, when a child's behavior threatens expulsion, an on-call early-childhood coach, so licensed slots stay open and parents keep their jobs.
customer: Licensed family child care providers (solo operators; start with about 300 in one metro or state). Co-payers: state agencies and child-care resource and referral (CCR&R) organizations with workforce-support funds, employers buying backup-care value, and Head Start partners.
problem: Childcare deserts are as much a retention problem as a construction problem. Family homes were the fastest-growing supply (+4.3% in 2024, versus +1.5% for centers), but one sick day closes a solo business, providers work 50-60 hour weeks, and average childcare worker pay is $33,140. Behavior challenges lead to expulsions, and few early-childhood mental health consultants exist to help. Each lost slot means a parent leaves work.
solution: 1) 'Slot Guarantee': a bench of background-checked, trained substitutes (retired teachers, early-education students, displaced parents) dispatched via app on a 2-hour target. 2) 'Calm Team': early-childhood coaches supervised by an infant-mental-health-endorsed clinician, deployed for observation and a behavior plan before expulsion. 3) Monthly Provider Circles of about 8 providers for peer support and reflective supervision. 4) Light back-office (attendance, billing).
why_now: Employer and family demand for childcare is rising with the 45F credit (40-50%) and the $7,500 dependent-care FSA, but supply is thin and fragile. Family homes are the growth segment, so protecting them is the cheapest new capacity. States are already funding workforce supports and early-childhood mental health consultation.
revenue_model: Provider membership of $79-129/mo including a few sub days per quarter, with extra sub hours billed at about $22/hr plus a fee. State or CCR&R contracts per provider. Behavior-coach visits at about $150 each or covered by state mental health consultation funds. Employer backup-care pools.
non_obvious_insight: Every desert plan builds new slots. The cheaper win is stopping existing slots from closing over sick days, burnout and expulsions. The real unit of childcare supply is a provider's mental state, and support for it is a bench of people, not an app.
first_30_days: Recruit 30 providers in one metro through Facebook groups and a CCR&R newsletter with a $59 founding-member rate. Assemble 15 substitutes from retired teachers and early-education students. Partner with one infant-mental-health clinician to lead the first Provider Circles. Approach the local CCR&R or county for a pilot fund, and track closures avoided as the headline metric.

title: Blank-First Microplastics: Clean Kits and Data Forensics
one_liner: Sell certified low-shed sampling kits, blank/spike proficiency samples, and legacy-data re-analysis to microplastics labs whose glove-contaminated numbers are now in doubt.
customer: Environmental testing labs pursuing state microplastics accreditation, public water utilities that must test and report, university microplastics groups, and beverage/bottled-water QA labs. Litigation and NGO teams that need defensible numbers are a secondary buyer.
problem: Routine nitrile and latex gloves shed stearate particles that read as microplastics, adding about 2,000 false-positive signals per mm² in University of Michigan tests. Labs are 'searching for the needle in the haystack' and are unsure how much of their existing data is contaminated. Labs cannot reliably tell real microplastics from consumable-derived artifacts.
solution: 1) 'Blank-first' kits with characterized cleanroom gloves, pre-cleaned filters, slides and foil, plus lot-level FTIR/Raman shed certificates. 2) Blind spiked reference samples for inter-lab proficiency checks. 3) A data-forensics service that re-screens a lab's archived spectra and micrographs for stearate signatures, using the published discrimination approach. 4) A public 'shed scoreboard' of glove and consumable brands to build trust and inbound leads.
why_now: The Michigan glove-artifact paper appeared in RSC Analytical Methods in 2026, and it says affected datasets can potentially be recovered. California's drinking-water microplastics program (SB 1422) has adopted IR and Raman methods and plans four years of testing and reporting. Its 22-lab intercomparison flagged accuracy and precision as needing improvement, so lab demand for defensible negatives is rising just as the artifact becomes public.
revenue_model: Consumable kits at roughly $300-1,000 per kit with recurring lot replenishment. Proficiency-sample subscriptions at roughly $2-5k per lab per year. Fixed-price legacy-data re-analysis packages at roughly $5-25k, and certification-lot fees.
non_obvious_insight: In a measurement crisis the money is in negative controls, not in a better detector. The demand evidence is the University of Michigan finding of ~2,000 false positives/mm² from ordinary gloves and 'thousands of times higher than expected' counts (https://www.sciencedaily.com/releases/2026/03/260329222938.htm). California's inter-laboratory study also says methods need better accuracy and precision through training and refinement (https://www.waterboards.ca.gov/drinking_water/certlic/drinkingwater/microplastics.html). Every lab that ever wore nitrile gloves has a reason to buy reassurance, and the researchers themselves say old datasets can be salvaged, which creates a service market.
first_30_days: Buy about 10 glove brands, filters and slides, and run shed tests through a university core-facility FTIR or Raman instrument to produce a public shed scoreboard. Write to the paper's authors and about 30 accredited environmental labs and utility QA managers. Sell the first 10 pilot kits at cost-plus and offer 2-3 discounted forensic re-analyses in exchange for case studies.

title: Protein Cartridges for Heavy Rare-Earth Polishing
one_liner: Skid-mounted cartridges of engineered lanmodulin-type proteins that separate heavy rare earths (Dy, Tb) from magnet-recycling leachate without long solvent-extraction chains.
customer: Magnet recyclers and small separators whose processes end in mixed rare-earth concentrates, plus DoD- and DOE-backed pilot programs.
problem: Recovery projects often end with mixed concentrates that still need separation, which conventionally takes hundreds of solvent-extraction stages that China dominates. Heavy rare earths are the acute chokepoint after China's 2025 export controls.
solution: Protein-based sorbents (naturally lanthanide-binding proteins, studied at Penn State and Lawrence Livermore) engineered for heavy-RE selectivity. They are packed in modular columns as a polishing step at ambient conditions. The business model is cartridge consumables plus skid rental.
why_now: Heavy rare earths are now a stated national-security bottleneck, DOE announced $134M for demonstrations in June 2026, and AI protein design has made engineering selectivity a computation problem instead of a decade-long screen.
revenue_model: Consumable cartridge sales plus skid lease. Early revenue from SBIR grants and paid pilots.
non_obvious_insight: Rare-earth chemistry fights in a sea of near-identical ions, while proteins evolved to tell lanthanides apart. The hard part is now designing the scaffold, not discovering the effect.
first_30_days: License or partner with a university lab. Run bench tests on real recycler leachate. Apply to DOE and DoD SBIR programs. Sign 2 recyclers to paid pilots.

title: Failed-Part Bounty for Insurance Subrogation
one_liner: Pay plumbers a bounty to bag, photograph and chain-of-custody the pipe, supply line or fitting that failed, then sell the evidence and a brand-level failure database to insurers' subrogation units and manufacturers.
customer: Subrogation departments and subro vendors at regional and mutual homeowners insurers (the ones too small to send a forensic engineer to a $9k supply-line loss). Second buyers: plumbing manufacturers, distributors and private-label buyers who license the failure data.
problem: Water damage is among the top two homeowner claim categories. Product-defect subrogation (a supply line, PEX fitting, toilet connector, ice-maker line or water heater that failed early) only works if someone kept the failed part. The plumber is on scene 1 to 3 days before the adjuster, cuts the failed piece out, and tosses it in the truck-bed scrap bin. When the adjuster arrives the evidence is gone, the insurer eats the loss, and the manufacturer's lawyers cite spoliation. Insurers only hire the $2,000 forensic engineer on the big losses, so the routine $8-15k losses are never pursued. Meanwhile every plumber knows which brands are failing (certain plastic-nut braided lines, certain fill valves, certain fitting lots) but nobody aggregates it.
solution: A 90-second protocol and kit. Tamper-evident bag with a QR label, a phone flow (photo of the part in place, photo after removal, the manufacturer stamp or date code, homeowner e-signature by text, and the claim number if one exists). A weekly courier pickup from the shop and a climate-controlled evidence locker. Optional one-page factual cause-of-loss statement drawn from the same photos (sudden burst versus long-term seepage, which is exactly the 'gradual leak' exclusion that decides whether homeowners get paid). Every part is logged by brand, model, date code and failure mode, which builds a Backblaze-style public failure-rate report by product line. Insurers get the part plus a ready evidence package. The shop gets a bounty and a small line item on the invoice.
why_now: Water-loss severity has risen sharply and carriers are under pressure on homeowners loss ratios, so they are hunting for recovery dollars. Copper and steel tariffs plus the shift to PEX and imported fittings have flooded the market with cheaper components of unknown quality. Photo and OCR tooling now makes a cheap, standardized evidence workflow possible, and the subrogation trade press is openly saying evidence preservation is the make-or-break step.
revenue_model: Insurer or subro vendor pays $75-150 per part with a documented chain of custody, of which $40-60 goes to the shop and tech. Plus a 3-8% success share on any recovery that follows. Plus annual data licenses ($15-60k) to manufacturers, distributors and big-box private-label buyers, and per-report fees for expert-witness-ready packages.
non_obvious_insight: The evidence that decides tens of millions in recoveries is currently destroyed daily by the only people who touch it first, and the reason is not malice. Nobody pays a tech to spend 4 minutes and a bag on a piece of scrap. The plumber, not the adjuster, is the true first-notice-of-loss for the product itself. The bounty is a price signal, and the dataset that falls out is one nobody else can buy.
first_30_days: Recruit 10 shops through a local PHCC chapter and the owner Facebook and peer groups with a flat $50 per bag and a free kit. Design the label and the phone flow in a form tool. Collect the first 50 parts with photos. Take the first 20 case files to two regional mutual insurers and a subrogation vendor and ask them which they would have pursued. Sell a paid pilot for 100 parts on the strength of their answers.

title: Reefer Claim Vault for Small Carriers
one_liner: An always-on evidence recorder that captures the proof that decides cargo claims, giving small carriers and their cargo insurers a one-click defense packet.
customer: Small reefer and dry-van carriers (1 to 50 trucks), especially produce and protein lanes, and the cargo-insurance agencies and MGAs that write them. Brokers needing reefer-specific carrier diligence are a secondary buyer.
problem: Small carriers lose or pay $5k to $60k cargo claims not because they were at fault but because they can't prove it. Pre-cool temperature, setpoint, continuous versus cycle-sentry mode, who loaded and counted, and seal integrity all decide a Carmack claim, and the evidence is usually never captured or gets overwritten on the reefer unit. After a claim, the cargo insurer raises rates or cancels. Post-Montgomery, reefer-specific vetting is also becoming a standard-of-care question for brokers.
solution: A driver app with a 90-second guided pickup ritual: photo of the empty trailer floor and reefer display, pre-cool temp, setpoint and mode, seal photo before the forklift touches it, an OCR check of the BOL that flags a missing 'SL&C' (shipper load and count) notation, seal number or temp instructions, and a Bluetooth probe reading of product temperature at load. It pulls continuous temperature records from reefer telematics (Thermo King, Carrier) or a $30 BLE data logger and hash-timestamps everything. When a claim lands, it generates a Carmack-structured defense packet in one click. Insurers get aggregate loss-prevention scoring by carrier.
why_now: The 2026 Montgomery ruling has brokers and insurers paying attention to reefer diligence. Cargo losses and theft are up sharply (Verisk CargoNet Q2 2026 losses of $304.6M). Vision AI makes BOL and photo checking cheap, and reefer telematics APIs and cheap Bluetooth loggers have matured.
revenue_model: $25 to $40 per truck per month for carriers. MGAs and agencies pay $10 per truck per month or fund the subscription in exchange for loss-ratio improvement and premium credits. A $150 flat fee per claim-defense packet for non-subscribers as a low-friction entry.
non_obvious_insight: Claims are decided by paper nobody produced in the sixty seconds when it mattered. Every veteran knows the ritual: write SL&C on the BOL, photograph the seal before anyone touches the door, snap the pre-cool, and download the reefer unit before it rolls over. Nobody does it consistently because nobody reminds them at the dock. Insurers see the losses but not the cause, so they will pay to change driver behavior at the moment of pickup.
first_30_days: Partner with 2 small cargo-insurance agencies that specialize in trucking. Recruit 20 reefer carriers hauling produce (Fresno to Nogales, Yakima, Salinas). Give them a free 30-day pilot plus the BLE logger at cost. Build a PWA using photo capture and Claude vision for BOL checks. Track claim outcomes on pilot trucks versus a control group to build the insurer's business case.

title: A Teaching Hospital Inside a Dead Hospital
one_liner: Lease a wing of a closed hospital and run it as a full-scale simulation hospital that nursing schools rent by the student-day.
customer: Community-college ADN and BSN programs turning away applicants, state workforce boards, and health systems that want a new-grad pipeline.
problem: Nursing schools turned away a record 93,176 qualified applications in 2025 (AACN, May 2026). The binding constraint is clinical placement sites, plus faculty vacancies above 7%. Many state boards allow up to 50% of clinical hours in high-fidelity simulation, but most school sim labs are a few beds in a converted classroom. Medicaid cuts are pushing more rural hospitals to close.
solution: Lease a closed hospital floor that already has medical gas, patient rooms, nurse stations, ICU bays and an OR. Fill it with liquidation beds and mannequins. Staff it with simulation faculty and local standardized patients such as retirees and theater students. Run immersive multi-day, 12-hour shift simulations from admission to discharge, sold per student-day or by semester cohort. Design to NCSBN and INACSL standards and get state board sign-off.
why_now: The record turned-away numbers landed in May 2026. 38 state boards had specific simulation rules by 2021 and more have followed. Rural closures are rising with the 2025 federal Medicaid cuts, so vacant, fully plumbed buildings are appearing cheaply. The $10B/yr Rural Health Transformation funds (FY26-30) create state workforce money to pay for seats.
revenue_model: $150-300 per student-day, or cohort contracts of $40-120k per semester per program. Health-system sponsorship for pipeline seats. Workforce and state grant funding.
non_obvious_insight: Simulation labs fail from unrealistic space and thin faculty, not from a lack of mannequins, and a dead hospital is the only building that already is the environment, priced at less than replacement cost. The buyer is a school with a waitlist, backed by employers and state money that want more graduates.
first_30_days: Pick two states with permissive simulation rules and long nursing waitlists. Call ADN program directors at 10 community colleges and offer a paid 2-day 'shift-in-a-day' pilot. Identify 3 closed hospitals through state health-department lists. Recruit a retired nurse educator as clinical lead, rent mannequins for a pilot, and charge $12-20k per cohort.

title: Independent Battery Safety Review for Counties
one_liner: Sell counties and fire marshals a developer-funded third-party plan review, hazard analysis and first-responder plan for every battery project.
customer: Storage developers pay the fees, usually through a county-controlled escrow. Counties and fire authorities contract the reviewer, and insurers use the dossiers.
problem: US storage installs hit a record 18.9 GWh in Q2 2026. After the January 2025 Moss Landing fire, hearings turn hostile and local moratoria spread. Fire departments lack expertise, NFPA 855 and UL 9540A data are hard to interpret, and developers lose 6-12 months in permitting.
solution: An independent safety dossier: hazard mitigation analysis, interpretation of large-scale fire test data, an emergency response plan, a thermal and off-gas monitoring plan and training for local responders. Sell it as fixed-price packages with an annual inspection option, plus a model county ordinance and review checklist.
why_now: Record installs are moving into populated areas, moratoria and insurer repricing are active, and code cycles are updating.
revenue_model: $25-80k per project via the county escrow, $5-10k a year for inspections, and training contracts.
non_obvious_insight: The bottleneck is trust, not technology. A reviewer the county chooses but the developer pays, like a planning consultant, speeds approvals and removes the NIMBY veto.
first_30_days: Draft a model BESS review ordinance and checklist. Offer free reviews to three counties with pending applications. Get two developers to pay for pre-application dossiers. Retain a fire-protection PE and a retired fire marshal.

title: Fall Response Network for Meteorite Hunters
one_liner: Rapid strewn-field prediction plus standard landowner-permission contracts and a fresh-fall sales channel for meteorite hunters, extendable to satellite-debris reentries.
customer: Serious hunters and dealers (subscription), landowners and park districts (permission desks), and buyers of fresh-fall specimens.
problem: The 17 March 2026 Ohio fall drew swarms of hunters, with pieces going for roughly $400-500 per gram early on, while a golf club closed its property and a park district warned hunters off. Permission takes days, fresh-fall value decays fast, and there is no standard revenue share with landowners.
solution: Alerts within 30-60 minutes combining public bolide and radar data with hobby camera networks and automated strewn maps. A pre-registered hunter roster with waivers, a standard landowner-share contract signed digitally, on-site chain of custody, classification via a partner lab, and consignment to dealers and museums.
why_now: The Ohio fall made the economics and the access conflict public. Open satellite and radar data and cheap all-sky cameras exist, and Starlink reentries add a second, insurer-relevant use case.
revenue_model: $20/month alerts, 10-15% of specimen sales, landowner-desk fees from park districts and insurers, and data licensing.
non_obvious_insight: Strewn-field maps are already published free, so the scarce thing is access and legitimacy in the first 72 hours. A contract-and-permission layer turns hostile landowners into revenue partners and creates an exclusive right-of-entry that cannot be scraped.
first_30_days: Build a 200-person hunter Discord and draft a standard landowner agreement. Test it on the next reported fireball with 20 landowners, and sign 2 dealers to buy through the network.

title: Corner-Shop Human Fallback for Age Assurance
one_liner: A network of licensed retailers that check ID in person and mint reusable, privacy-preserving age credentials, sold to age-assurance vendors and platforms as the human appeal layer.
customer: Age-assurance vendors and platforms (social, gaming, adult, gambling, app stores) that face false rejections. Retailers such as independent pharmacies, post offices, newsagents, liquor stores and credit unions earn per credential.
problem: Facial age estimation has error bands near the threshold, so borderline users (16-18, and adults who look young) are blocked. Adults with expired or mismatched ID are locked out. The appeals queue is expensive support, and the legal exposure is real: Australia's under-16 social media law, in force since December 2025, carries fines up to A$49.5 million, and the UK's Online Safety Act requires highly effective age assurance.
solution: Partnered counters run a clerk app. The customer shows government ID, the app reads the chip by NFC without retaining an image, and it issues a reusable over-13, 16, 18 or 21 credential to the person's phone wallet, or a code for those without a smartphone. Platforms and vendors route estimation failures and borderline users to the nearest counter or a video-call agent through one API. Audit logs, retailer training and mystery-shop QA back the process.
why_now: Australia's guidance treats reusable age credentials, vouching and trusted third-party attestation as acceptable methods. California's app-store age assurance law takes effect on January 1, 2027, and UK enforcement has expanded through 2026. Every platform is discovering that automated estimation needs a human fallback.
revenue_model: The vendor or platform pays $0.75-2.50 per rescued user, and the retailer keeps about 40%. Add cents per reuse verification, and enterprise contracts for fallback capacity.
non_obvious_insight: Regulators demand highly effective age assurance, but nobody has built the cheap human appeal layer. Licensed retailers are already trusted age checkers for alcohol, tobacco and medicines. The network of humans is the moat, not the cryptography, and it earns as long as automated estimation is imperfect.
first_30_days: In one Australian metro, sign 40 independent pharmacies and newsagents. Build the clerk app on an open-source NFC reader for passports and licenses. Pitch two age-assurance vendors on a white-label fallback and charge per rescued user for a 60-day pilot. Track false-reject recovery rate as the headline metric.

title: Distressed Cargo Rescue Desk for Bankrupt Importers
one_liner: A broker-run desk that takes orphaned containers from failed importers, clears the four-way legal tangle in days, and delivers the goods to off-price buyers at deep discounts.
customer: Off-price retailers, closeout buyers and liquidators who cannot currently buy orphaned cargo because they are not the consignee. Carriers and CFS operators, who want the boxes gone, and trustees, who want recovery, are the supply side. The buyer pays a handling fee or a spread.
problem: When a small importer fails mid-shipment, the goods sit on the water or on a terminal with no ISF, no entry, no bond and a demurrage and storage clock running. The bills of lading are in a dead company's name. Carriers and warehouses will not release cargo to strangers. Buyers would pay well for the goods but cannot make entry. Unentered cargo can be sent to a General Order warehouse after about 15 days and is subject to public sale after roughly six months, so value bleeds out. Many boxes are eventually abandoned, auctioned for pennies or destroyed. The 2025-26 tariff whiplash left a long tail of failed importers, and Long Beach's record volumes keep yard space and free time expensive.
solution: Run a cargo rescue desk with five steps. (1) Source: call carriers' demurrage collection desks, CFS warehouses in Carson and Long Beach, and bankruptcy trustees to find orphaned cargo. (2) Screen: triage compliance risk (CPSC certification, FDA, FCC, UFLPA and IPR issues) and refuse any box that cannot be legally sold. (3) Title: obtain the trustee's or owner's transfer of cargo rights and a negotiated carrier release, trading the removal of the box for a waiver or reduction of demurrage. (4) Entry: the purchaser, as an actual purchaser with the right to make entry, becomes importer of record on a single-transaction bond, with a licensed broker filing the entry. (5) Deliver to the buyer's warehouse. Where the invoices are non-compliant, a dispute of the demurrage under the FMC's billing rules adds leverage.
why_now: Small-brand failures peaked through the 2025 tariff shock and its aftershocks. The IEEPA reversal of Feb 2026 has estates now holding refund cash but still holding stranded physical goods. Off-price retail demand for cheap inventory is high. Single-transaction customs bonds mean a new team does not need a continuous bond or big capital to start.
revenue_model: 10-15% handling and sourcing fee on landed cost from the buyer, or a resale spread on consignment goods. Add trustee-side success fees where the desk increases estate recovery. Duties and fees are pre-funded by the buyer, so the desk avoids inventory risk in the early phase.
non_obvious_insight: A container of orphaned goods is worth its inventory value minus the clock. The party that can solve four separate systems (bill-of-lading rights, the carrier lien and demurrage, customs entry and IOR, and compliance screening) in days captures the discount. VCs treat liquidation as a marketplace problem. It is a legal-plumbing problem, and only a customs broker knows how the entry, bond and purchaser-as-IOR pieces fit together.
first_30_days: Line up a partner bond agent for single-transaction bonds and one buyer network of 5-10 off-price and closeout buyers. Call demurrage collections and terminal-side contacts at 10 carriers and 10 CFS warehouses with a simple offer: we clear abandoned cargo if you waive charges. Ask two bankruptcy trustees whether any estate holds cargo. Close the first 2-3 rescues in the 30-60 day window with fully buyer-funded duties.

title: Trade-Crew Capacity Forward Book for Builders
one_liner: A 12-week forward view of subcontractor crew availability for regional homebuilders, giving small builders the trade-partner visibility that Lennar has in-house.
customer: Regional builders and general contractors doing 50-800 homes a year in Texas, Florida and the Southeast, which pay a monthly subscription. Framing, drywall, landscape, paving and electrical subs join free.
problem: Labor availability is turning into a constraint in specific trades and regions. Lennar says roughly 20% of its divisions are under greater pressure from localized immigration enforcement and data-center construction, and crews vanished with little notice (landscaping was the example). Paychex reports its blue-collar clients cannot find electricians. Small builders can't see 3-4 months ahead the way Lennar's purchasing teams do, so a crew that disappears becomes a delayed closing.
solution: A weekly text or WhatsApp pulse asks each sub for crew size, planned availability by week, licensing and insurance status, and a lawful-workforce attestation such as E-Verify participation. The data rolls up to a builder dashboard showing committed versus needed crew-days by trade and community, with alerts when a sub's committed capacity drops. A shared bench lets builders pool vetted backup crews in the same metro, with a per-placement fee. The pitch is schedule continuity. Compliance data is a by-product.
why_now: Enforcement and the data-center construction boom are hitting trade labor at the same time as builders' closing cycle times are at record lows (116 days at Lennar). Builders are compressing schedules just as crews get less predictable. Starts are down, which gives builders leverage today but makes them dependent on retaining subs when volume returns.
revenue_model: $400-$1,500/month per builder division, plus a $150-$400 fee per successful backup-crew placement, plus a paid insurance-and-attestation verification tier for subs.
non_obvious_insight: The winner's edge at scale is information, not labor supply. Lennar's Jim Parker says purchasing teams 'have tremendous visibility with our partners' and can 'allocate their crews to where we need them', with 3-4 months of crew visibility, while Stuart Miller says 'labor availability has started to become more of an issue', citing 'localized immigration enforcement and data center construction' and landscaping crews as the example (https://www.fool.com/earnings/call-transcripts/2026/09/17/lennar-len-q3-2026-earnings-call-transcript/). Paychex's CEO says clients 'are having trouble finding people ... a need for a lot of electricians and construction work' (https://www.fool.com/earnings/call-transcripts/2026/09/24/paychex-payx-q1-2027-earnings-call-transcript/). KB Home sees no labor problem today, so the risk is regional and uneven (https://www.fool.com/earnings/call-transcripts/2026/09/23/kb-home-kbh-q3-2026-earnings-call-transcript/). A large builder's advantage is a relationship graph, which small builders can rebuild cheaply with a weekly text poll. It should be pitched around schedule continuity.
first_30_days: Pick one metro (for example DFW or Tampa) and one trade (landscape or framing). Recruit 3 regional builders and 25-40 subs via builder purchasing managers. Run the weekly text pulse manually with a shared Google Sheet and Twilio, and deliver a Monday capacity report by email. Charge $500/month from week 4 on a 90-day pilot. Vet legal language on workforce attestations with an employment lawyer before launch.

title: Medicare-First Longevity Kit for Independent Practices
one_liner: Longevity medicine built on what Medicare already pays for, sold as a workflow kit to independent primary-care practices.
customer: Independent primary-care and DPC-adjacent practices (2-15 clinicians) with 500-2,000 Medicare patients each.
problem: The longevity boom (Function $2.5B, Neko ~$7B, Superpower up to $349/yr) targets cash-paying under-55s, while the highest-risk group, seniors, has a covered prevention stack that is badly under-used. Well under half of beneficiaries take the Annual Wellness Visit, and independents lack the workflow to turn covered services into a healthspan program.
solution: A configurable 'healthspan AWV' template with functional tests (chair-stand, grip, gait speed), cognitive and falls screens, covered lipid, diabetes and bone screening, and vaccine gap-closing. A monthly care-management billing layer (APCM codes introduced in 2025). Compliant ABN-based cash upsells for ApoB or Lp(a). Practices get scripts, patient handouts and a collections dashboard.
why_now: APCM monthly primary-care codes are new (2025). The Medicare GLP-1 Bridge began Jul 1, 2026, pulling seniors into metabolic care. Cash longevity prices keep rising, which cedes the 65+ segment. About 82% of doctors are employed, so the remaining independents are underserved by digital vendors.
revenue_model: $600-1,200/month SaaS per practice plus 15-20% of incremental collected revenue (est. $30-80k per clinician per year of newly captured billing).
non_obvious_insight: 'Longevity' for the 65+ is mostly a billing-and-workflow problem on already-covered benefits. Founders build for cash because that is where the venture buzz is, and they overlook the biggest and sickest demographic, whose payer is already at the table.
first_30_days: Recruit 5 independent practices via state IPAs and DPC-Medicare communities. Offer a free 30-day audit of their AWV and care-management capture, pulled from claims, showing dollars left on the table. Convert to a $499/month pilot with a success fee.

title: Incretin-in-a-Drop Assay for Life Underwriting
one_liner: A dried-blood-spot or oral-fluid lab test that tells insurers whether an applicant is actually on semaglutide, tirzepatide, orforglipron or retatrutide.
customer: Life and disability insurers, reinsurers, MGAs and paramedical exam vendors, with bariatric programs, trial sponsors and outcome-based employer programs as follow-on buyers.
problem: Cash-pay and direct-ship fills (LillyDirect, NovoCare, telehealth-partner pharmacies, compounders, gray market) are only partly visible in claims-based Rx histories, so BMI looks 'preferred' while drug-supported. Stopping the drug means rebound and adverse selection. Gray-market retatrutide is invisible by design.
solution: A validated LC-MS/MS panel (semaglutide, tirzepatide, orforglipron, cagrilintide, retatrutide) run by a partner CLIA lab as an add-on to the paramedical exam, returning 'on-board, recent use or none'. Later expansions to pre-op verification, adherence-verified outcome contracts and a consumer 'proof of adherence' report.
why_now: Published LC-MS/MS methods for semaglutide and tirzepatide matured in 2026, the FDA's LDT rule was vacated in 2025, and cash-pay pill volume exploded in 2026 (Wegovy pill >2M scripts).
revenue_model: $25-45 per test as an underwriting add-on, volume tiers for carriers, and later $79 consumer or clinician tests.
non_obvious_insight: This is the first mass-market chronic drug that bypasses the industry's data plumbing. Underwriters will pay for direct measurement over questionnaires because the cost of a wrong mortality class is far above $35.
first_30_days: Ask two Rx-history vendors what share of DTC fills they see. Contract a CLIA tox lab to validate an assay from published methods. Pitch 10 MGAs and reinsurer innovation teams, and run a paid 200-sample blinded pilot with one friendly insurer, with consent and state unfair-discrimination rules reviewed by counsel.

title: Continuity Vault for Solo Operators
one_liner: A break-glass vault, dead-man switch and runbook so a solo business survives its owner's hospitalization or death, and its AI agents stop cleanly.
customer: Solo and two-person business owners aged 45+, reached through independent life-insurance agents, estate attorneys, SBA lenders and CPAs.
problem: For the majority of small businesses that are solo operations, the owner is the only person with access to the bank, domain, Google listing, payroll, customer list and payment processor. When the owner is incapacitated, nobody can legally or technically act. Delegated AI agents and OAuth tokens add new failure modes because they keep acting, or fail, without supervision.
solution: An encrypted vault with a named successor, dead-man switch, and pre-authorized runbook: the top ten bills, customer notification templates, who to call, how to pause automated agents and revoke tokens, and a wind-down-or-sell pack with a handoff to a route or book sale.
why_now: Owners increasingly hand credentials to AI agents and automations, and the 2026 loosening of SBA lending (7(a) plus 504 up to $10M) makes lenders care about key-person risk. The boomer owner cohort is aging.
revenue_model: $199 setup plus $19/month direct, wholesale at $99 per client to advisors, and API licensing to lenders.
non_obvious_insight: For the smallest businesses, succession usually means continuity, not sale. The distributor is the person who sells the life policy, who needs a reason to call every client each year.
first_30_days: Recruit five independent insurance agents or estate attorneys and offer white-label onboarding for 50 clients. Test whether successors can complete a simulated break-glass drill in under an hour.

title: Notice Red-Team and Pleading Triage for Landlords
one_liner: An adversarial checker that tries to break every eviction notice before it is served, then triages incoming AI-drafted pleadings and prices cash-for-keys exits.
customer: Mid-size operators (500-10,000 units) and the landlord-tenant law firms that serve them on flat-fee matters.
problem: Federal pro se filings topped 41,000 in 2025 against a 23,000 average for 2005-2022, and one tenant filed 22 pleadings in a weekend. Operators pay outside counsel to triage each one while units sit idle, and some conclude cash-for-keys is cheaper than winning. Tenants' AI can find a defective notice in minutes, so procedural errors are now fatal.
solution: An adversarial reviewer checks each notice (cure periods, statutory language, service method, ledger accuracy including banned fees) against jurisdiction rules before service. Inbound pleadings are classified, deadlines docketed, and a 48-hour decision brief compares cost-to-contest with a benchmarked cash-for-keys offer that respects relocation rules. An evidence pack (ledger, communications, inspection logs) is auto-assembled. Licensed attorneys supervise, to avoid unauthorized-practice risk.
why_now: Generative tools have made pro se filings cheap and voluminous, and operators are shrinking staff and leaning on AI leasing, so their record-keeping is thin. Municipal fee bans add new ways a ledger can be wrong.
revenue_model: $3-6 per unit per year platform fee plus $75-250 per triaged matter; law-firm seats at $300-600 per month.
non_obvious_insight: The real cost is not the pleading but the vacant unit while it sits in dispute, so the winning metric is decision speed inside 48 hours. Both sides are now AI-armed, and the defensible edge is an adversarial 'red team' that finds your process defects before the tenant does.
first_30_days: Partner with two landlord-tenant firms in a high-volume market. Build a notice checker for two jurisdictions and run it free on 200 historical notices to show catch-rates. Convert firms to a $500 per month seat and operators to a per-matter fee.

title: Grid-Paid Spiffs for Water Heater Installers
one_liner: Make the plumber on the emergency water-heater call the distribution channel for heat pump water heaters and grid demand-response programs, with a same-day rebate stack, an electrician handoff and a per-device bounty paid to the tech.
customer: Virtual power plant aggregators, utility demand-response and efficiency-program administrators and manufacturers' connected-water-heater programs, who pay for enrolled devices. The plumbing shop and tech are the paid channel partners.
problem: Roughly 9 million water heaters get replaced each year and the large majority are emergency replacements decided in a four-hour window, standing in an inch of water. The plumber decides what goes in. Utilities and aggregators spend hundreds of dollars per customer on mailers and rebates that almost nobody uses, because the customer does not think about the water heater until it dies. Plumbers install the 50-gallon tank on the truck because a heat pump unit needs a 240V circuit, a condensate drain, clearance and paperwork, plumbers do not do electrical, and a callback eats a week of margin. The federal 25C credit ended December 31, 2025, so what is left are state and utility rebates that customers cannot pre-approve while the old tank is leaking.
solution: An install-day tool for the tech's phone. Enter the ZIP, the current heater and a photo of the panel and get back every stackable rebate for that address with the homeowner's net cost against a like-for-like tank (a 20-second sales conversation). Route the 240V circuit to a pre-priced partner electrician for a next-day flat fee, or steer to a 120V plug-in heat pump model when the panel is tight. At install, scan the QR on the heater to enroll it in the aggregator or utility program with the customer's consent. Pay the tech a same-week spiff and the shop a fee. We handle rebate paperwork in the background so the plumber's job ends when the tank is set.
why_now: Federal tax credits are gone, so utility and state programs and point-of-sale rebates now decide the price difference. Virtual power plants and utility demand-response are actively looking for cheap, high-volume device enrollment. Manufacturers now ship connected and 120V plug-in heat pump units that remove the biggest install objections. The labor-constrained plumber has never been offered a spiff that is bigger than the hassle.
revenue_model: Take 20-30% of the per-device enrollment or midstream incentive paid by the aggregator or utility (typically $200-600 per device is now spent on customer acquisition), pay $50-100 to the tech and $50-100 to the shop, and keep the rest. Add a per-install electrician referral fee and a $99 per month shop subscription for the rebate engine once volumes justify it.
non_obvious_insight: The whole electrification industry markets to homeowners, who make no decision until the tank fails. The only person who actually decides is a plumber with a 20-minute window, paid by the ticket and hating callbacks. Plumbers will not sell a heat pump water heater because it is a worse day for them, not because they are anti-green. Fix the day and the channel opens, and the spiff is the cheapest customer acquisition the grid will ever buy.
first_30_days: Choose one territory with a live heat pump water heater rebate plus a demand-response or VPP program (e.g. Massachusetts, Colorado, the Pacific Northwest or California). Build the rebate stack for that utility in a spreadsheet and a text-message enrollment link. Sign 5 shops and 1 partner electrician. Pitch an aggregator or the program administrator a pilot of 100 enrolled devices at an agreed bounty, with the spiff paid manually at first.

title: Break-Glass Interim Operators for Deceased Owners' Businesses
one_liner: An on-call bench of laid-off COOs and ops directors who step in within 48 hours when the sole owner of a small business dies, keeping it alive until the heirs can sell or close it.
customer: Estate attorneys, CPAs, SBA lenders and key-person insurers who need the business to keep its value, plus the widow or heirs. The estate ultimately pays from business cash flow or sale proceeds. Target businesses: HVAC and trades firms, machine shops, independent insurance agencies, restaurants and other 5-50 employee owner-dependent companies.
problem: Probate treats assets as inert (houses, accounts), but a running business melts within 90 days when the owner dies: bank signing authority, payroll, licenses, customer relationships and key employees all hinge on one person. Executors are grieving family. Attorneys cannot run a company. Brokers cannot sell one in freefall. Boomers still own a large share of employer businesses, so this is a huge, mostly invisible transfer.
solution: A vetted bench of interim managers with a 72-hour playbook: secure bank and payroll access via letters testamentary or a special administrator, notify customers and vendors, fund key-employee retention from the estate, arrange licensing 'qualifier' coverage where required, stabilize for 60-90 days, prep a data room, then hand off to a broker or buyer. AI tools (contract abstraction, bookkeeping analysis, KPI dashboards) let a newcomer understand the business in about a week. Owners can pre-buy a 'continuity plan' retainer.
why_now: The largest generational transfer of small businesses is under way (Cerulli: $124T through 2048, about 81% from Boomers and older), while the 2026 labor market is full of experienced ops leaders who cannot find roles. Cheap AI document and finance tooling makes fast onboarding of an unfamiliar business feasible for the first time.
revenue_model: Interim GM day rate of $900-1,500 billed to the estate, with the bench member keeping about 65%. Pre-need continuity retainer of about $1,200/yr for solo owners. Success fee on a sale, in coordination with brokers.
non_obvious_insight: The estate needs a verb, not a noun. The legal system has a process for distributing what a person owned but none for continuing what a person did. Unemployed senior operators are the perfect supply for that verb, and their downside is only the awkwardness of arriving during grief.
first_30_days: Recruit 15 laid-off ops and finance leaders. Write the 72-hour playbook. Offer a free 'owner-death readiness check' at bar association and CPA society events for 30 attorneys and accountants. Sell a $1,200/yr continuity retainer to 20 solo-owner businesses through one insurance agency or SBA lender's client list. The first at-need engagements will come from those attorneys' existing clients.

title: The Weekly Mail Box for Mom
one_liner: A prepaid return envelope where a parent drops all her mail. It gets scanned, triaged, shredded, and turned into a 'what needs doing' digest for her adult child.
customer: Adult children aged 45-62 with a parent 75+ living alone, often 100+ miles away. Secondary customers are daily money managers, professional fiduciaries and elder-law firms who currently collect and read mail by hand.
problem: Paper mail is where scams (fake invoices, 'prize fees', Medicare plan pitches), real bills and the notices that cost money arrive: property-tax exemption renewals, Part D changes, IRS notices, Medicaid paperwork. Kids discover the unopened shoebox at Thanksgiving. USPS Informed Delivery shows only the exterior of some letter-size mail. Parents refuse apps, dashboards and shared passwords because that feels like surrender.
solution: A weekly pre-addressed return flat that the parent fills with the whole pile, with no sorting. The team scans it, uses AI to classify and extract sender, amount, due date and required action, flags likely scams (any 'send a check to claim your prize' letter), and calls or texts the parent for urgent items ('Do you want the water bill paid?'). The child gets a weekly digest and a dashboard. Originals are shredded or returned monthly, per the parent's choice. Over time it builds the 'where everything is' paper trail that estates need: accounts, policies, pensions and annuities.
why_now: Cheap, accurate AI document extraction only became affordable at consumer prices in the last two years. Treasury phased out paper checks on Sept 30, 2025, and agencies are pushing digital, while seniors still get paper notices. Older-adult scam losses run in the billions per year (FTC). Medicare open enrollment begins Oct 15, so the mailer flood is imminent.
revenue_model: $49/month per household (about $14 in postage, scanning and AI, for roughly 70% gross margin). $25 per household per month wholesale for daily money managers and fiduciaries. Optional $149 one-time 'estate paper trail' report.
non_obvious_insight: Seniors will turn down every dashboard, but they will hand over an envelope pile happily, because mailing is a ritual they own. The pile is the real system of record for a widow's finances. Scam checks and wire requests are usually triggered by letters, so scanning the inside of the envelope catches what exterior-only tools cannot. Children do not want passwords either. They want to know what to pay.
first_30_days: Recruit 30 households in one metro through caregiver Facebook groups, local AARP caregiver meetings and elder-law attorneys. Run it manually with a $500 duplex scanner, an AI extraction pipeline and a retired teacher doing quality checks. Charge from day one. Track 'catches' (scams intercepted, missed notices found) and publish them. Then pitch daily money managers.

title: Laid-Off Managers Buy Retiring Owners' Funeral Homes
one_liner: A matchmaker, training cohort and SBA-loan packager that pairs displaced mid-career operators with retiring owners of independent funeral homes, so local homes stay local and the buyers get AI-proof, trust-based work.
customer: Buyers: laid-off director- and VP-level ops, HR, finance and customer-experience people aged 38-55 with severance, savings or a 401(k) rollover for a down payment. Sellers: independent funeral-home owners aged 60+ with no child taking over (NFDA counts 15,401 US funeral homes, about 75% family or privately owned).
problem: Owners have no succession plan, and their realistic exit is a consolidator (SCI, Everstory and others) that dissolves the local name and pushes preneed. White-collar workers hit by the hiring freeze (Amazon cut about 16,000 corporate roles in Jan 2026; information-sector jobs fell 23K in Aug) cannot find durable human-presence work. Licensing rules and deal mechanics make the path opaque.
solution: A 10-week 'Director-Owner Program': state-by-state licensing roadmap (many states let an unlicensed owner run a home if a licensed director-in-charge is employed, but verify each state), a 6-12 month paid apprenticeship placement inside a partner home before closing, FTC Funeral Rule and preneed-trust training, and SBA 7(a) plus seller-note structuring. Add confidential seller listings and matching. After closing, a shared ops kit (software, price-list compliance, vendor rates) and a peer board of owner-operators.
why_now: SCI's Q2'26 results (preneed sales +7%, operating cash flow +43%, volume -1.4%) show value is in pricing and preneed, not volume, so well-run independents are valuable. Cremation is heading to about 82% by 2045, which lowers facility needs. Consumer interest in green options (61.4%) gives new owners a differentiator that legacy owners ignore. Displaced managers are abundant now.
revenue_model: Buyer tuition of about $4,500 (partly deferred to close). Seller-side success fee of 1.5-3% or $15-25K. Deal-packaging fee of about $5K. Owner-community subscription of $199/mo. Later: software and preneed-admin services.
non_obvious_insight: The funeral-home succession gap and the mid-career white-collar glut are the same problem seen from two ends. The best buyer is a people-good operator, not a financier, and consolidators structurally cannot serve either side: they overpay for scale and cannot preserve local identity. It is the ultimate trust job, and AI cannot hold a widow's hand.
first_30_days: Choose two states with friendly licensing and many rural homes. Phone 100 owners aged 60+ via the state funeral-directors association, aiming for 5 signed no-cost 12-month 'successor search' agreements. Recruit the first 10 buyers from laid-off-manager communities (ex-Amazon alumni groups, LinkedIn, Blind) with a $500 refundable screening deposit. Pre-qualify with one SBA lender. Start 1-2 apprenticeships at partner homes.

title: LOMA Rescue for Newly Flood-Mapped Homeowners
one_liner: Door-to-door service that gets newly mapped flood-zone homeowners an elevation certificate and a FEMA map amendment (LOMA) package before they are forced into flood insurance, with surveyors paying for the leads.
customer: Homeowners whose parcels were just moved into FEMA high-risk zones, who pay $600-900 for an elevation certificate plus filing. Licensed surveyors pay $75-150 per booked job, and private flood MGAs pay referral fees for owners who do not qualify.
problem: Thousands of homes were newly mapped into Special Flood Hazard Areas. Mandatory purchase kicks in fast, and change notification is not mandatory, so many owners learn from a lender letter. Many do not know that a home whose lowest adjacent grade sits above the base flood elevation can petition out. A one-time survey cost competes with a permanent premium annuity plus escrow increases.
solution: A parcel-level tracker of FEMA map-change communities, with screening from public elevation and LiDAR data. We mail and door-hang targeted homeowners with a fixed-price 'get out or get covered' offer. We book a vetted surveyor, file the LOMA package, and route non-qualifiers straight to private flood quotes (referral fee) and mitigation contractors.
why_now: Cotality reports (2026-09-18) that new FEMA maps put thousands of homes into high-risk zones across 100+ communities in 12 states. Homeowners must secure cover within 45 days, and for 10% of homeowners escrow already exceeds principal and interest. NOAA's flood inundation mapping reached nearly 100% of the US population in September 2026, which raises public awareness of flood exposure.
revenue_model: Flat $700-1,000 homeowner package split with the surveyor (about 25-30% margin), plus $50-150 referral fees on private flood or NFIP binds for non-qualifiers. Later sold as a white-label to title companies and community lenders.
non_obvious_insight: The 'uninsurable' problem is here solved by contesting the map, not by finding a carrier. Evidence from https://www.carriermanagement.com/news/2026/09/18/292073.htm: the top newly mapped communities are Escambia County FL (2,344 properties), Pender County NC (678), Chattanooga TN (635), Ithaca NY (428) and Methuen MA (428). The article says change notifications are not mandatory, leaving some homeowners uninformed, and that homeowners have 45 days to secure flood insurance. About 4,500 named parcels in five communities is a concrete addressable list with a hard deadline and no dominant consumer-facing service. Only owners with grade above base flood elevation qualify, so the model needs screening and an honest fallback.
first_30_days: Pull the parcel lists for the five named communities from county GIS and FEMA change notices. Pre-screen elevations with public LiDAR. Sign 2 local licensed surveyors on per-job pricing. Mail 1,000 letters or door hangers in Escambia and Pender with a fixed price and a free eligibility check. Target 20-30 booked certificates in the first month.
